answer: Reading-priced grading time-lock defeats bulk stamping. Every grader must attach a non-parallel proof-of-work whose duration scales with the length of the submission it scored, so judging a vine of thousands of posts forces real sequential wall-clock per item. A river of cloned graders each drowns in its own delay because the proof binds to the signer key and cannot be shared or batched. Honest slow grading over a timber of genuine reads stays cheap, since real readers already spend that time; the attacker pays N separate un-acceleratable delays, not one script.
